_note: What node tools/check_lock_scope.mjs --self-test must see when it scans this directory. The fixtures are the guard's only proof that its two silent rules (the helper rule, the same-mutex re-lock rule) still fire: a clean run on the real tree reads identically whether those rules work or have rotted. Label matching is by substring, so a reworded rule message does not silently disable its own test — it fails the build until the expectation (and the fixture's // expect: comment) is brought along.

flagged.why: the callee's body is in cross_tu_helper.cpp and reaches the PAL; a file-local scan cannot see it, so this is the expectation that proves the whole-tree index is doing the work
a locked method calls a sibling that locks the SAME mutex object — same class, non-recursive mutex, so the thread waits on a lock it already holds

quiet.why: same shape on a std::recursive_mutex, whose whole purpose is a second acquisition by the same thread
the callee locks ANOTHER class's equally-named mutex_ — same name, different object
the callee's name has two definitions in scope, so the call must be reported as unresolved rather than guessed at (see unresolvedMin)
the blocking body itself: reached only through cross_tu_caller.cpp, and holding no lock of its own
one of the two definitions of the ambiguous name
the other definition of the ambiguous name; resolving to either one would be a guess
